NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, and 2521, due to the continuing state of emergency, including
  masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is
  being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person in the Council
  Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling 1-669-900-6833 from any phone, Meeting
  ID: 815 4073 3031, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using
  the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 815 4073 3031, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 13, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:06 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), due to the continuing state
of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of
the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by the following members of 4H Club: Sophie Loewner, Emily Aye, Irbrahim Yaaseen,
Eisa Yaaseen, Timmy Keese.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING SEPTEMBER "NATIONAL PREPAREDNESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR ZERUNYAN declared September 2022 “National Preparedness Month.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-I AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF AUGUST & SEPTEMBER 2022

  APPROVED WARRANTS S 65413 THROUGH 65515 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $327,174.86; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080622; 090122
  THROUGH 090322; 65449 (VOID); IN THE AMOUNT OF $106,523.31; FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $433,698.17 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 13, 2022
 D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 22, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 30, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  DRAFT PALOS VERDES PENINSULA PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE AND
  REGIONAL CONTRACT LAW COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  RESOLUTION NO. 2527 ESTABLISHING DIRECTOR OF COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT AND DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC WORKS JOB CLASSIFICATIONS
  AND DESCRIPTIONS WITHIN THE MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEE GROUP

  ADOPTED  RESOLUTION  NO.  2527  ESTABLISHING  THE
  CLASSIFICATIONS AND JOB DESCRIPTIONS FOR THE DIRECTOR OF
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC WORKS
  WITHIN THE MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEE GROUP.

H.  POLITICAL REFORM ACT REPORTING REQUIREMENTS/CITY CONFLICT OF
  INTEREST CODE

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2528 WHICH ADOPTS BY REFERENCE
  THE CURRENT FAIR POLITICAL PRACTICES COMMISSION STANDARD
  MODEL CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODE, DESIGNATES POSITIONS
  REQUIRED TO SUBMIT STATEMENTS OF ECONOMIC INTEREST AND
  DEFINES THE DISCLOSURE CATEGORIES.

I.  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2529 WITH HdL COMPANIES TO SUPERSEDE
  RESOLUTION NO. 2526

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2529 AUTHORIZING HDL TO EXAMINE
  SALES AND PROPERTY TAX INFORMATION WITH THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF TAX & FEE ADMINISTRATION (CDTFA) AND LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY TREASURER AND TAX COLLECTOR.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public comment related to the Promenade and the Palos Verdes Performing Arts (PVPA)
was received by: Tita Bougler, Julie Reynolds, Abby Douglass, John Sanders, Sue Soldoff,
Lara Hanlon, John Reynolds, Steve Goldberg, and Kelly Evans.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY ACTION ITEMS FROM AUGUST 30, 2022

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Traffic and Safety Committee’s
  recommendations to: 1.) Approve the attached Local Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP); 2.)
  Approve the installation of edgeline striping at the Peninsula Center Library driveway
  exit onto Deep Valley Drive to assist motorists away from the bulb-out; and 3.) Approve
  “KEEP CLEAR” markings on Palos Verdes Drive North at the intersection of Palos
  Verdes Drive North and Silver Saddle/Moccasin Lanes, in both west and east-bound
  directions.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 13, 2022
 Assistant Engineer of Willdan Engineering, Emilio Murga provided a presentation to the Council
on the Development of a Local Road Safety Plan (LSRP).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE ATTACHED LOCAL ROADWAY SAFETY PLAN (LRSP).

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated she supports the addition of the edgeline striping as
recommended.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF EDGELINE STRIPING AT THE
  PENINSULA CENTER LIBRARY DRIVEWAY EXIT ONTO DEEP VALLEY
  DRIVE TO ASSIST MOTORISTS AWAY FROM THE BULB-OUT.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba noted that there are other “KEEP
CLEAR” markings in a number of locations on Palos Verdes Drive North, including at
Dapplegray Lane, in response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE “KEEP CLEAR” MARKINGS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH
  AT THE INTERSECTION OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND SILVER
  SADDLE/MOCCASIN LANES, IN BOTH WEST AND EAST-BOUND
  DIRECTIONS.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

B.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: DAPPLEGRAY LANES SPEED
  HUMP SURVEY

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the installation of two speed humps
  on Buckskin Lane at a cost not to exceed $10,000.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired if the residents of Buckskin Lane were informed of
the results of the survey, and that they are the only street getting speed bumps. Community
Development & Public Works Director Wahba confirmed the results were sent to their
Homeowners Association.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 13, 2022
   MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF TWO SPEED HUMPS ON BUCKSKIN
  LANE AT A COST NOT TO EXCEED $10,000.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: TURF REPLACEMENT
  PROJECT FINAL DESIGN AND COST PROPOSAL

  Recommendation: That City Council approve the final designs and specifications for
  the Turf Replacement projects located at City Hall grounds and Highridge Park, and
  the Bennett Landscape cost proposal as a task order to the existing contract at a cost
  of $84,668 for City Hall and $135,000 for Highridge Park, which is fully funded by
  California Water Service reimbursable rebate program

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Manager Grammer noted that due to the short timeline to be eligible for the rebate
program, the decision was made to work with the City’s existing contractor Bennett
Landscaping under the current contract, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked staff, CalWater, and the Land Conservancy for their
partnership in this project.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE FINAL DESIGNS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR THE TURF
  REPLACEMENT PROJECTS LOCATED AT CITY HALL GROUNDS AND
  HIGHRIDGE PARK, AND THE BENNETT LANDSCAPE COST PROPOSAL AS
  A TASK ORDER TO THE EXISTING CONTRACT AT A COST OF $84,668 FOR
  CITY HALL AND $135,000 FOR HIGHRIDGE PARK, WHICH IS FULLY
  FUNDED BY CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE REIMBURSABLE REBATE
  PROGRAM.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER (VERBAL
  REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that there has been no change to the Los Angeles County
Department of Public Health’s Order, that daily positivity and hospitalization rates are declining,
and Los Angeles County has now moved down to the low transmission level. He added that
updated booster shots are now available for those 12 years and older.

City Manager Grammer also reported on a letter that the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified
School District signed onto with several other Los Angeles County school districts asking that
the Los Angeles County’s Health Order be consistent with the State’s Health Order as it relates
to masking. They have asked the local cities to support them in this request. There has been
a response by Los Angeles County Department of Public Health stating that no changes were
going to be made at this time.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 13, 2022
 10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported on the League of California Cities’ Annual Conference and
Expo she and the rest of the Council attended in Long Beach last week.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also attended the Palos Verdes Chamber of Commerce’s Legislative
Committee meeting this afternoon.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN announced that the 65th Annual City Celebration would
take place this Saturday, September 13, at the Empty Saddle Club.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:21 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting in honor of Joe
Esquivel and Glenn Zack. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, September 27, 2022, at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Frank V. Zerunyan
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 13, 2022
